(a) a particle swarm model of organizational adaptation, which includes a degree of strategic inertial, is capable of simulating the adaptive behavior of a population of organizational agents, and (b) a particle swarm organizational model with strategic inertial can outperform a particle swarm organizational adaptation model without strategic inertial, in a static and slowly changing environment.

the presence of strategic inertia, coupled with a degree of agent (organization) ignorance of the payoffs associated with potential strategies, is beneficial to the adaptation of the average strategic fitness of a group of organizations.
the presence of strategic inertia in an organizational population, when combined with an election mechanism, can lead to a higher level of adaptive fitness than is possible in the absence of inertia.

the results indicate that a degree or strategic inertia, in combination with a democratic election mechanism, can improve the adaptive performance of a population of agents (organizations) in static and slowly-changing environments.

strategic inertia is an adaptive mechanism that is most effective when the strategic environment is changing slowly and when the organizations in the population are able to assess accurately the potential payoffs of potential strategic alternatives.
